findings.title: The final adoption commit and recovery workspace remain outside the exact path boundary
findings.reproduction: The strict-descendant candidate correctly constrains candidate-to-REVIEW, REVIEW-to-disposition, and approved-state-to-adoption-evidence commits, but neither gcrctl nor taskctl derives and validates the later commit that records the canonical ADOPTED state and revision-7 backlog. In a temporary real-Git lifecycle, the remediated controller completed adoption; the resulting backlog and state were then committed together with planning/hidden-final-adoption.txt. The commit's name/status delta was M planning/backlog.yaml, M planning/governance-control-recovery/GCR-0001.B00.state.json, and A planning/hidden-final-adoption.txt, yet gcrctl.validate_state_history returned successfully and hidden_final_adoption_commit_accepted=True. A second temporary lifecycle stopped immediately after transaction publication, created unrelated-untracked.tmp, and invoked recover_adoption_transaction. Recovery returned COMPLETED_SUCCESSOR while the unrelated file survived, producing dirty_recovery_accepted=True. recover checks branch, trigger witness, transaction authority, and canonical record hashes, but it does not deny unrelated staged, tracked-worktree, or untracked paths. These paths can therefore coexist with completion of the exact governance transition, contrary to acceptance criterion 8's direct-child exactly-two-path adoption commit, the packet's every-extra-path denial, and its clean Git identity prohibition.
findings.requiredRemediation: In a strict-descendant R03 candidate, add a non-circular finalization invariant that derives the unique commit introducing the adopted backlog/state pair, requires it to be the direct child of the exact adoption-evidence commit, requires the complete no-renames name/status delta to be exactly M planning/backlog.yaml and M planning/governance-control-recovery/GCR-0001.B00.state.json, and verifies both Git blobs against the live successor bytes before any adopted generation is accepted by gcrctl or taskctl. Before that commit exists, expose only a fail-closed pending-finalization state and deny downstream recovery-supplement use. Add a specialized recovery workspace guard that permits only the hash-bound trigger witness, the exact canonical transaction artifacts, and canonical backlog/state bytes at a declared predecessor/successor boundary; deny every other untracked path, every staged path, and every unrelated tracked worktree change before cleanup or roll-forward. Add real-Git tests for hidden/substituted final adoption commits and for untracked, staged, and unrelated tracked dirty recovery attempts. Preserve R01 and R02 append-only, submit fresh R03 evidence, and explicitly close this finding before revision 7 is usable.

closures.evidence: Candidate 22f9b46dd6772d2df615d3324cd1797f585385f8 derives the canonical approved state from the latest immutable ledger; exact single-parent no-renames status/path comparisons bind candidate-to-REVIEW, REVIEW-to-disposition, and approved-state-to-adoption-evidence commits and their Git blobs. Independent replay confirmed hidden reviewed-state, hidden approved-state, hidden adoption-evidence, and substituted-parent commits are denied before transaction preparation.

Candidate 22f9b46dd6772d2df615d3324cd1797f585385f8 replaces the unjournaled sequential write with schema-bound durable successor payloads, a write-ahead manifest, Windows MoveFileExW replace-existing/write-through publication, cross-reader transaction/split-state denial, and idempotent explicit recovery. Independent replay passed all seven child-process abrupt boundaries: unpublished payloads restore the exact predecessor; a published transaction completes the exact successor; marker-deleted split state fails closed; and all canonical transaction artifacts are removed after recovery.
